texts.facts: The present suit has been initially filed under Order XXXVII of Code of Civil Procedure (in short CPC) seeking recovery of Rs.6,13,190/- from the Defendant alongwith interest. However, in view of separate statement made by Ld. Counsel for the Plaintiff, the present suit was converted into an Sh. Ashwani Kumar vs M/S Bee Gee Catering Private Limited on 3 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149742891/ 1 Ordinary Civil Suit. 1.1 Facts as averred in the plaint are that the Plaintiff is the Sole Proprietor of Shudh Garhwal Paneer Nirmata Sangh, which is engaged in the business of distribution, manufacturing and supplying of milk and other milk products such as ghee, dana khoya, cooking cream, paneer, butter, cheese etc. It is stated that Plaintiff has been engaged in this business for past 27 years and is a distributor and supplier to numerous Five Star Hotels and Government Bodies of India. It is stated that the Plaintiff holds the requisite license from the Food Safety & Standards Authority of India to carry out his business. It is stated that the present suit is being filed through Mr. Manik Saha, Junior Manager, who was authorized vide Authorization letter dated 17.04.2017. It is further stated that Defendant is engaged in the business of catering services. It is stated that in March, 2011, the Defendant approached and made representation for purchase, supply and delivery of milk and various milk products to be supplied and delivered to the addresses i.e. (i) Chelmsford Club, 1-Raisina Road, New Delhi, (ii) 2 nd Floor, 214-216, S.F. DDA Commercial Complex, Aurobindo Place Market, Hauz Khas, New Delhi; and (iii) C-600, Defence Colony, Delhi, where the Defendant company was providing catering services. It is stated that as per the representation made by the Defendant, the Plaintiff agreed to supply milk and various milk products on various dates as per day to day demands and requirements of the Defendant company at the aforesaid venues. It is stated that the Defendant company agreed that upon supply and delivery of products by the Plaintiff, any concerned person or employee of Defendant would sign/stamp and acknowledge the delivery of products to which the Plaintiff would raise consolidated monthly invoices at the end of the month. It was further agreed that the invoices raised by the Plaintiff would be cleared within 15 days from its receipt and failure to pay or clear the invoice would attract and accrue interest @18% p.a. It is stated that as per the requirements of the Defendant, the Plaintiff started supply of milk and milk products to Defendant from April, 2011 onwards at the venues. It is stated that the present suit is filed with respect to the outstanding dues for the products supplied at venue Chem's Ford Club, 1 Raisina Road, New Delhi. It is stated that the challans are acknowledged by the staff/ employee of the Defendant company namely Sh. Rahul, Sh. Rajendra, Sh. Vinod Kumar and Sh. Saurabh, who were present at the said venue at the time of delivery of products by the Plaintiff. It is further stated that milk and milk products supplied and delivered by the Plaintiff were as per the various requirements and demands placed upon the Plaintiff from time to time and produces were received by the Defendant as per their satisfaction and never returned to the Plaintiff as defective product. It is stated that from April, 2011 till February, 2013, the Defendant company had placed numerous orders on the Plaintiff which the Plaintiff delivered without delay and compromise on the quality of its products. It is stated that on the basis of signed/ stamped and acknowledged challans by the employees of the Defendant company, the Plaintiff raised consolidated invoices which were duly acknowledged by the Defendant company. It is stated that the Defendant initially made payments on the invoice value but later on the Defendant started making on account payments. It is stated that from April 2011 to February 2013, the Plaintiff had supplied products worth Rs.38,27,318/- at the Chemsford Club, for which challans and invoices were raised from time to time. It is stated that the Plaintiff made last supply to the Defendant on 06.02.2013 vide Challan no. 02/13/AA2866 at the aforementioned venue and the Plaintiff raised last consolidated invoice on the Defendant on 06.02.2013 bearing Serial no. TI- 16260 for a sum of Rs.1,215.90/-, which was still outstanding and due and payable. It is stated that thereafter, the Plaintiff was constrained to stop supplying the milk Sh. Ashwani Kumar vs M/S Bee Gee Catering Private Limited on 3 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149742891/ 2 and milk products at all the venues of the Defendant. It is stated that the Defendant made part payments of the invoices from 01.03.2013 till 19.12.2015 and the Defendant company made an account part payment of Rs.10,000/- on 19.12.2014 towards invoices. It is stated that on 28.04.2015, the Defendant issued a cheque no. 135772, drawn on Corporation Bank for a sum of Rs.50,000/- which returned back dishonoured. It is further submitted that an admitted sum of Rs.6,13,190/- alongwith interest @18% p.a. was still outstanding, due and payable by the Defendant to the Plaintiff. It is stated that the Plaintiff repeatedly contacted the Director of the Defendant company and requested him to clear the outstanding amount but the Defendant sought extension of time and evaded its liability. It is stated that the Plaintiff issued a legal notice on 11.09.2016 upon Defendant company calling upon it to pay an amount of Rs.9,13,460/- alongwith interest @18% p.a. till its realization. It is stated that the said legal notice was for consolidated amount dues qua all the venues where the Plaintiff supplied the products to Defendant company. On these grounds, the present suit is filed seeking recovery of Rs.6,13,190/- alongwith interest from the Defendant. 2. Summons of the suit were issued to the Defendant. Upon service of summons, the Defendant appeared and filed its written statement. It is stated in the written statement that the present suit is without any cause of action; that the plaint has not been verified as per law; that the suit has not been filed by the duly authorized person. It is stated that the Plaintiff was seeking recovery of Rs.6,13,190/- on the premise of having allegedly supplied various materials, however, none of the bills produced by the Plaintiff had any acknowledgment of materials being supplied. It is stated that unilateral raising of invoices including the last invoice of 06.03.2013 was only a ploy to bring the present suit within the period of limitation. It is further stated that none of the invoices were accompanied with the orders to support said invoices. It is stated that the alleged payment of Rs.10,000/- on 19.12.2014 and issuance of cheque dated 28.04.2015 were manipulated documents as blank signed cheques were given by the Defendant to the Plaintiff at the time of entering into business proposals in 2011-2012. It is stated that Defendant had made payments of all the invoices through which the material was supplied to Defendant and after the settlement of all invoices, the Plaintiff had made a false claim upon the Defendant. All other pleadings made in the plaint were denied by the Defendant. PW1 Sh. Manik Saha tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A and placed reliance on certain documents viz. Authorization letter Ex. PW1/1, company's master data Ex.PW1/2, delivery challans from 01.09.2012 to 31.12.2012 Ex. PW1/3 to Ex. PW1/85, cheque no. 135772 dated 28.04.2015 Ex.PW1/86, legal notice Ex. PW1/87 and postal receipts & AD cards Ex. PW1/88 and Ex. PW1/89. Since none appeared for the Defendant despite opportunities, the cross-examination of PW1 was closed being Nil vide order dated 13.04.2022. Even this witness was not cross-examined on behalf of the Defendant despite repeated opportunities and cross-examination of PW2 was closed being Nil vide order dated 28.09.2022. Further, an application under Order XVIII Rule 17 CPC was moved for recalling of evidence for the purpose of exhibition of Certificate under Section 65 B of Indian Evidence Act. The application was heard and allowed on 31.01.2023. PW-1 Manik Saha has placed on record Certificate under Section 65 B of Indian Evidence Act Ex.PW-1/90 and PW-2 has also placed on record certificate under Section 65 B of Indian Evidence Act Ex.PW-2/15. 6. The Plaintiff has also placed cheque of Rs.50,000/- dated 28.04.2015.

The Hon'ble Division Bench of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Pt. Munshi Ram & Associates (P) Ltd. v. DDA, 2010 SCC Online Del 2444 has held that higher rates of interest, which are against public policy, can be struck down by the Court by finding such rates of interest to be against the pub- lic policy. Any Contract, which is against the public policy, is void under Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. The said Judgment was also relied upon by the Hon'ble Single Bench of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case bearing R.F.A No. 823 of 2004 titled as Shri Sanjay Mittal Versus Sunil Jain decided on 07.12.2018. The Hon'ble Single Bench has granted 9% per annum interest instead of 24 % per annum i.e. 2% per month. 13. In the considered opinion of this court, the interest of 24% per annum as claimed is unreasonable and excessive in terms of the Judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and is also against public policy and void under Section 23 of the In- dian Contract Act, 1872.
